attempted_claim: Let X be an isotropic, log-concave random vector in R^n with Var(|X|^2) = 8n. Prove (or disprove) that the law of X is a rotation of the i.i.d. centered-exponential product: there exist O in O(n) and i.i.d. Z_1,...,Z_n with common density e^{-(t+1)} 1_{t >= -1} such that X =d OZ.
decisive_failure: No complete proof or disproof of the rigidity claim was obtained. The 1D fourth-moment bound (value 9) was only probed numerically, not proved with a uniqueness statement; the n-dimensional equality analysis via stochastic localization or KLS localization was not developed; Monte Carlo and grid-quadrature evidence is approximate with truncation and sampling error; and no exhaustive search over isotropic log-concave measures was possible.
